==English== ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|folwen}}, {{m|enm|folȝen}}, {{m|enm|folgen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|folgian||to follow, pursue}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*folgēn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fulgāną||to follow}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈfɒləʊ/|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈfɒlə/|a=Northumbria}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈfɔlo/|a=Scotland}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈfɑloʊ/|a=GenAm,dialects of Canada}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-follow.ogg|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|a=colloquial,folk speech,nonstandard|/ˈfɑlə/}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈfɒloʊ/|a=CA,dialects of the US}} * {{hyphenation|en|fol|low}} * {{rhymes|en|ɒləʊ|s=2}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} [[File:What_about_us,_then%5E_-_geograph.org.uk_-_2548341.jpg|thumb]] # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[go after]]; to [[pursue]]; to move behind in the same path or direction, especially with the intent of catching. #: {{syn|en|trail|tail}} #: {{ant|en|guide|lead}} #: {{ux|en|'''Follow''' that car!}} #: {{ux|en|She left the room and I '''followed'''.}} #* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|system=PC|scene=Citadel|genre=[[science fiction|Science Fiction]]|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|passage=Ambassador Udina: The other species are scared. They've never faced anything like this before and they don't know what to do. They want us to step forward. They believe in humanity because of you.
Ambassador Udina: Your ruthless pursuit of Saren and the geth, your defiance of the Council -- that's what humans are capable of! That's how we can defeat the Reapers!
Ambassador Udina: The others will '''follow''' us, Shepard. They know we're their only hope. We will have a human Council with a human Chairman.}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To go or come after in a sequence. #: {{syn|en|succeed|Thesaurus:succeed}} #: {{ant|en|precede|Thesaurus:precede}} #: {{ux|en|B '''follows''' A in the alphabet.}} #: {{ux|en|We both ordered the soup, with roast beef to '''follow'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=23 June 1532|last=Trychay|first=Sir Christopher|authorlink=Christopher Trychay |quotee=Will[ia]m Scely|title=The cownte of Willm Scely beyng Wardyng of ye almys|location=w:Morebath|newversion=republished in|compiler2=R. Erskine Binney, B.A.|title2=The Accounts of the Wardens of the Parish of Morebath, Devon, 1520-1573|year2=1904|publisher2=James G. Commin|location2=w:Exeter|page2=39|pageurl2=https://archive.org/details/devonandcornwal01unkngoog/page/n53|passage=Where a pon thys for sayd men dyd sett ye prysse under ye maner as here after '''follyzth''': & Thomas Borrage yt was tuthyng man at ye tyme for iak Tymwell dyd gether ys mony yt '''follyth''' & brosth hyt to ys for said men by causse yt they schuld se every man content after their conssyens|translation=Consequently, these aforesaid men set the prices in the manner that hereafter '''follows''', and Thomas Borrage, who was tithingman at the time for Jack Tymwell, gathered this much that '''follows''' and brought it to these aforesaid men so they could have everyone content according to their conscience.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[carry out]] (orders, instructions, etc.). #: {{syn|en|pursue}} #: {{ux|en|'''Follow''' these instructions to the letter.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|IV|pages=58–59|pageref=58|passage=The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track.{{...}}Their example was '''followed''' by others at a time when the master of Mohair was superintending in person the docking of some two-year-olds, and equally invisible.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To live one's life according to (religion, teachings, etc). # {{lb|en|transitive}} To understand, to pay attention to. #: {{ux|en|Do you '''follow''' me?}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[watch]], to [[keep track of]] (reports of) some event or person. #: {{ux|en|I '''followed''' the incumbent throughout the election.}} #: {{ux|en|My friends don't regularly '''follow''' the news.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To be a [[supporter]] of (a sports team). #* {{RQ:Bramah Bravo of London|passage="Sometimes I wonder what you do take any notice of—except the whistle and short skirts," speculated his superior. "But no doubt ideas are germinating."
"I '''follow''' Chelsea," maintained Horace.}} # {{senseid|en|subscribe to content}}{{lb|en|social media|transitive}} To [[subscribe]] to see [[content]] from an [[account]] on a [[social media]] platform. #: {{ant|en|unfollow}} #: {{ux|en|If you want to see more of our articles, '''follow''' us on Twitter.}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To be a logical consequence of something. #: {{syn|en|ensue}} #: {{ux|en|It '''follows''' that if two numbers are not equal then one is larger than the other.}} #: {{ux|en|If you don't practise proper hygiene, illness is sure to '''follow'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To walk in, as a road or course; to attend upon closely, as a profession or calling. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Twelfth Night|I|iii|256|2|passage=O had I but '''followed''' the Arts.}}
